newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - Dollar/mark vols rise on spot strength.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Dollar/mark vols rise on spot strength.

text.p: Implied volatilities for dollar/mark options rose sharply Tuesday after the dollar climbed against European currencies overnight.
However, dollar/yen volatilities retreated as the dollar also gained ground against the Japanese currency, pulling farther away from last week's 111.98 yen low.
Pressure on the mark stemmed from fresh jitters over European monetary union prospects after the left's victory in the first round of French legislative elections Sunday.

The dollar was further underpinned in U.S. trading by a surge in U.S. consumer sentiment to a 28-year high. The Conference Board's consumer confidence index leaped to 127.1 in May, far exceeding the forecast of 114.4 and sparking a sell-off in the bond market.
Options traders said dollar/mark volatility was well-bid on the back of the spot's push above 1.70 marks.
"In dollar/mark, there is fresh bullish sentiment in the dollar," said Masao Okada, chief dealer at Dai-ichi Kangyo Bank.

Dollar/mark 25-delta risk reversals remained skewed slightly toward mark calls at flat/0.2, but Okada predicted the bias would soon shift to reflect growing dollar bullishness. "It's just a matter of time until we see it reversed," he said.
One-month dollar/mark volatility rose 0.6 point from Friday to 9.6/9.8 percent, widening the inversion of the curve. One-year gained 0.3 point to 9.3/9.45 percent.
Traders said some market participants were buying dollar/mark volatility and selling dollar/yen volatility on a spread basis as values for the options moved in opposite directions.
One-month dollar/yen volatility declined 0.2 point to 11.5/11.7 percent and one-year edged down slightly to 10.4/10.5 percent.
The dollar was trading near 116.70 in the early afternoon.
Okada predicted the pullback in dollar/yen volatility would be short-lived.
"The offer side of dollar/yen is heavy. Everyone is afraid of a lower dollar/yen short term, so this is a correction," he said.
Traders said Japanese exporters were looking to buy one- to three-month yen calls and dollar puts in the 112 and 111 strikes, especially if the spot rises to 117.
Dollar/yen 25-delta risk reversals widened to 1.2/1.45 in favor of yen calls.
